stories.headline: Tennessee death row inmate survives attempted lethal injection
stories.body: Tennessee prison officials failed to execute death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday night. The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 20:00 local time. Hours before, the US Supreme Court cleared the way for her execution by lethal injection. Pike could have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years. The scheduled execution procedure involved two injections of pentobarbital. Two lethal injections failed to kill her. Her legal team filed an emergency motion after the procedure. They said Pike lost consciousness, still had a heartbeat, and was audibly snoring. District Judge Clifton L. Corker issued a ruling. He said medical personnel began giving medical care to Pike. Authorities treated Pike at a nearby hospital on October 1. Department spokesperson Dorinda Carter said officials followed state execution protocol. She said they moved Pike to an off-site medical facility. Dr. Joel Zivot said in an email that Pike will likely suffer a brain injury. He said this injury will come as a consequence of delayed resuscitation. Robin M. Maher of the Death Penalty Information Center spoke about execution survivals. She said no one has stayed alive after receiving lethal injection drugs. Pike was 18 years old when she killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995. She lured Slemmer into woods, cut her throat, and smashed her head with a rock. Police found a pentagram carved into Slemmer's chest. Pike's boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp got life in prison with the possibility of parole for his role in the murder.

claims.text: On October 1, Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike was treated at a nearby hospital after authorities failed to carry out her execution.
The attempted execution of Christa Pike took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 20:00 local time on Wednesday night.
Two lethal injections failed to kill convicted murderer Christa Pike during her high-profile execution.

Hours before the execution attempt, the US Supreme Court cleared the way for Christa Pike to be executed by lethal injection, making her potentially the first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years.
The scheduled execution procedure for Christa Pike involved two injections of pentobarbital.
Christa Pike's legal team filed an emergency motion stating she lost consciousness, still had a heartbeat, and was audibly snoring after receiving lethal injections.
District Judge Clifton L. Corker issued a ruling noting that medical personnel had begun administering medical care to Christa Pike.
Tennessee Department of Correction spokesperson Dorinda Carter stated that the department followed state execution protocol and transported Christa Pike to an off-site medical facility.
Dr. Joel Zivot stated in an email that Christa Pike will likely suffer brain injury as a consequence of delayed resuscitation.

Robin M. Maher of the Death Penalty Information Center stated seven people have survived medical problems from vein access failure during execution, but no one has stayed alive after receiving lethal injection drugs.
Christa Pike was 18 years old when she and her boyfriend killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp in 1995.
On January 12, 1995, Christa Pike lured Colleen Slemmer into a wooded area at the University of Tennessee, cut her throat with a box cutter, and smashed her head with a rock.
Colleen Slemmer's body was discovered with a pentagram carved into her chest.
Christa Pike's former boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp was convicted of first-degree murder in 1997 and sentenced to life with the possibility of parole for his role in Slemmer's death.

stories.headline: United States completes full military withdrawal from Iraq
stories.body: United States forces completed their military withdrawal from Iraq on September 30. This departure ended a military presence that began with the 2003 invasion. The final withdrawal followed a 2024 agreement signed between Washington and Baghdad. US forces left more than two decades after the invasion that overthrew Saddam Hussein. Iraq declared Sovereignty Day to mark the event. Iraqis celebrated with night-time events as a four-day national holiday began. Around 100 British military personnel also departed from Irbil on Wednesday. British forces left alongside US troops. The UK Ministry of Defence spoke about military strikes during Operation Inherent Resolve. It said Royal Air Force aircraft struck more than 2,300 ISIS targets in Iraq. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi spoke about the end of the coalition mission. He said Iraq now takes full responsibility for its own security and stability. US President Donald Trump wrote a message on Truth Social. He said the exit was a victory for the United States. He called it a victory for Iraq. He also called it a decisive victory over ISIS. A recent UN report assessed the strength of ISIS in Iraq. The report said counter-terrorism operations left ISIS with several hundred fighters. It said these fighters are only capable of unsophisticated operations. More than one million US service members served in Iraq during the first phase of the war. US troop levels reached about 170,000 personnel during the 2007 surge. The US Department of Defense recorded 4,419 military deaths during Operation Iraqi Freedom. It also recorded 31,993 military personnel wounded in action. Brown University's Costs of War project estimated war spending through early 2023. It said the US spent about $1.79 trillion on wars in Iraq and Syria. Abu Mujahid al-Assaf of Kataib Hezbollah spoke about the departure. He described the exit as the expulsion of occupation forces. He said it marks the beginning of full Iraqi sovereignty. The Iraqi government extended a deadline to negotiate disarming powerful Iran-backed militias. The new target deadline is June 2027.

claims.text: The United States completed the withdrawal of its remaining military forces from Iraq on September 30, ending a military presence that began with the 2003 invasion.
The final US military withdrawal from Iraq was carried out under a 2024 agreement signed between Washington and Baghdad.
The last U.S. forces left Iraq more than two decades after the U.S.-led invasion that overthrew Saddam Hussein, as Iraq declared Sovereignty Day.
Iraqis observed the start of a four-day national holiday with night-time celebrations to mark Sovereignty Day following the US troop departure.
Around 100 remaining British military personnel departed from Irbil in northern Kurdistan alongside US forces on Wednesday.
The UK Ministry of Defence stated that Royal Air Force aircraft struck more than 2,300 ISIS targets in Iraq during Operation Inherent Resolve.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi stated that the end of the coalition mission marks Iraq's transition to full responsibility for its own security and stability.
US President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that the troop exit was a victory for the United States, a victory for Iraq, and a decisive victory over ISIS.
A recent UN report assessed that sustained counter-terrorism operations left ISIS in Iraq with several hundred fighters capable only of unsophisticated operations.
According to the Council on Foreign Relations, more than one million US service members served in Iraq during the first phase of the war.
During the 2007 surge, US troop levels in Iraq reached approximately 170,000 personnel.
The US Department of Defense recorded 4,419 military deaths and 31,993 wounded in action during Operation Iraqi Freedom.
Brown University's Costs of War project estimated that the US spent about $1.79 trillion on wars in Iraq and Syria through early 2023.
Abu Mujahid al-Assaf of Kataib Hezbollah described the US military exit as the expulsion of occupation forces and the beginning of full Iraqi sovereignty.
The Iraqi government has extended the target deadline to negotiate the disarmament of powerful Iran-backed militias to June 2027.

stories.headline: Russia attacks Ukrainian energy grid in massive overnight strike
stories.body: Russia launched a massive combined air strike against Ukraine's energy grid overnight on Wednesday. The attack killed seven people across five regions. Ukrainian state grid operator Ukrenergo imposed emergency power cuts in Kyiv and three surrounding regions. This was the first time Ukrenergo used emergency cuts since spring. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke about Moscow's actions. He said Moscow is increasing pressure on civilians as winter approaches. He said Russia wants to turn cold and darkness into weapons. Russian strikes damaged the Trypilska thermal power plant. The plant sits roughly 40 kilometres from Kyiv. It is the largest supplier of electricity to the capital city. Kyiv Mayor Vitaly Klitschko said three people died in the capital during the strikes. He said the dead included a utility company worker at a warehouse building. Zanny Minton Beddoes of The Economist spoke about the strikes on Kyiv. She said Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment as Russia tries to make the city unlivable. A Russian attack drone crashed into a children's playground in Kyiv without exploding.

claims.text: Russia launched a massive combined air strike against Ukraine's energy grid overnight on Wednesday, killing seven people across five regions.
Ukrainian state grid operator Ukrenergo imposed emergency power cuts in Kyiv and three surrounding regions for the first time since spring.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that Moscow is increasing pressure on civilians as winter approaches to turn cold and darkness into weapons.
Russian strikes damaged the Trypilska thermal power plant, located roughly 40 km from Kyiv, which is the largest supplier of electricity to the capital.
Kyiv Mayor Vitaly Klitschko reported that three people were killed in the capital during overnight strikes, including a utility company worker at a warehouse building.
Zanny Minton Beddoes of The Economist stated that Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment as Russia attempts to make the city unlivable.
A Russian attack drone crashed into a children's playground in Kyiv without exploding.

stories.headline: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar stops mid-air attack on Flydubai flight
stories.body: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar saved a Flydubai flight after his co-pilot attacked him inside the cockpit. The incident occurred on September 30, 2026, on Flydubai flight FZ1073. The plane was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The aircraft transmitted emergency signals during the flight. It made a sharp descent of more than 17,000 feet from an altitude of 34,000 feet. The co-pilot stabbed Machchhar inside the cockpit. Officials said the stabbing was an alleged attempt to crash the plane. Israeli officials said the co-pilot accused of the attack is an Omani citizen. Machchhar sustained severe injuries during the assault. Despite his injuries, he activated the cockpit door release switch. This action allowed crew members and passengers to intervene. They stepped in to overpower the attacker. Passenger Yaniv Hayoun said he placed the attacker in a chokehold. He said he dragged the attacker out after catching him attempting to destroy instrument panels. Two off-duty Flydubai pilots travelling as passengers also stepped in. They assisted in overpowering the attacker. They also helped in diverting the aircraft. The plane diverted to Prince Sultan Bin Abdel Aziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. It was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children. The Israeli embassy in Australia confirmed that a Jewish couple from Sydney was on board. Israel's ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman spoke about the attack. He said it was an attempt to hit at peace established by the Abraham Accords. Flydubai temporarily suspended flights to and from Israel following the attack. Machchhar is a 50-year-old native of Mumbai. He spent 11 years with SpiceJet before joining Flydubai in 2022. Machchhar logged nearly 9,750 flying hours over a 15-year career. He primarily flew Boeing 737 aircraft. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Machchhar a hero. He said India is proud of him. President Droupadi Murmu commended Machchhar on X for his bravery and quick response. Airline SpiceJet praised Machchhar and said all of India is proud. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also called Machchhar a true hero.

claims.text: Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed inside the cockpit by his co-pilot during an alleged attempt to crash the Flydubai aircraft.
On September 30, 2026, Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv transmitted emergency signals and made a sharp descent of more than 17,000 feet from 34,000 feet.
According to Israeli officials, the co-pilot accused of stabbing Captain Smit Machchhar is an Omani citizen.
Despite sustaining severe injuries, Captain Smit Machchhar activated the cockpit door release switch to allow crew and passengers to intervene and overpower the attacker.
Passenger Yaniv Hayoun stated that he placed the attacker in a chokehold and dragged him out after catching him attempting to destroy instrument panels.
Two off-duty Flydubai pilots travelling as passengers stepped in to assist in overpowering the attacker and diverting the aircraft.
Flydubai flight FZ1073 diverted to Prince Sultan Bin Abdel Aziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, while carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children.
The Israeli embassy in Australia confirmed that a Jewish couple from Sydney was on board the diverted Flydubai flight.
Israel's ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman stated that the cockpit attack was an attempt to hit at the peace established by the Abraham Accords.
Flydubai temporarily suspended flights to and from Israel following an attack on a pilot.
Captain Smit Machchhar is a 50-year-old Mumbai native who spent 11 years with SpiceJet before joining Flydubai in 2022.
Before joining Flydubai, Captain Smit Machchhar logged nearly 9,750 flying hours over a 15-year career primarily flying Boeing 737 aircraft.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Captain Smit Machchhar a hero and stated that India is proud of him.
President Droupadi Murmu commended Captain Smit Machchhar on X for his bravery and quick response in preventing a major tragedy.
Airline SpiceJet praised Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, stating that all of India is proud.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Captain Smit Machchhar a true hero.

stories.headline: INDIA opposition bloc launches nationwide protests over Election Commission voter drive
stories.body: Leaders from 19 opposition parties in the INDIA bloc called for future elections in India to use paper ballots. The opposition bloc announced a series of nationwide protest actions. They announced a Save Democracy March from October 2 to October 8. They also planned a protest march to the Election Commission on October 6. They scheduled a meeting with President Droupadi Murmu. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned changes made to the online Form 6 voter registration form. He asked who at the Election Commission ordered Tata Consultancy Services to alter the form on the ECINET portal. Tata Consultancy Services handles core digital backend infrastructure for the Election Commission. An investigative report by The Indian Express revealed details about internal objections. The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to changes on the portal. Former Chief Election Commissioner O. P. Rawat said the Election Commission has lost credibility. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh cited Rawat as saying nearly 14 crore voters lost their voting rights through the Special Intensive Revision. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that the voter drive was a backdoor National Register of Citizens.

claims.text: Leaders from 19 opposition parties in the INDIA bloc called for future elections in India to be conducted using paper ballots.
INDIA bloc leaders announced a Save Democracy March from October 2 to October 8, a protest march to the Election Commission on October 6, and a planned meeting with President Droupadi Murmu.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi asked who at the Election Commission ordered Tata Consultancy Services to illegally alter the online Form 6 voter registration form on the ECINET portal.
Tata Consultancy Services handles the core digital backend infrastructure and ECINET portal management for the Election Commission of India.
An investigative report by The Indian Express revealed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections to changes made to the online Form 6 on the ECINET portal.
Former CEC O. P. Rawat stated that the Election Commission has lost credibility and that Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi should have done more to oppose improper decisions.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh cited former Chief Election Commissioner O. P. Rawat as stating that nearly 14 crore voters had been disenfranchised through the Special Intensive Revision.
AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that the Special Intensive Revision exercise was a backdoor National Register of Citizens.
